findings.section: How it works, subsection headings
findings.quote: ### A secondary Region takes over by failover after an outage by switchover when healthy (4 min)
findings.evidence: Without commas several assertion headings cannot be parsed at a glance by a second-language reader: this one, 'Data moves into Aurora by snapshot by Aurora read replica or by AWS DMS', 'The reader endpoint spreads connections not single queries across replicas', 'When the writer fails Aurora promotes a replica behind the same endpoint'. READER.md: 'Headings, tables and captions must give a correct gist on their own'; she 'trusts the gist she gets from one glance'. STYLE.md: one main idea per sentence. The exemplar headings stay readable without commas ('Same-account access needs one allow but cross-account access needs two'). Rephrase, for example 'After an outage you fail over and for a planned move you switch over', 'Three paths move data into Aurora: snapshot, Aurora read replica and AWS DMS' (if the colon is allowed in anchors) or 'The reader endpoint balances connections and not single queries'.
findings.resolution: Tried: lint L103 refuses commas in headings. A reworded heading changes its section id, which brief.json fixes (L905) and which verified questions, cards and speak items use as their section; changing it would break Q111/C108/P108 or reset verified questions. Logged for the orchestrator to change the brief headings in a later pass.

findings.section: Choose it or not, compare headings
findings.quote: ### Aurora Replica RDS read replica or Multi-AZ standby
findings.evidence: Read at a glance this is one long noun phrase; the three options cannot be separated without commas ('Aurora Replica, RDS read replica or Multi-AZ standby'). The same for '### Aurora RDS or DynamoDB' (reads as 'Aurora RDS'). READER.md: headings must give a correct gist on their own. Use 'Aurora Replica vs RDS read replica vs Multi-AZ standby' or another form the anchor rules allow.
findings.resolution: Tried the commas: lint L103 ('heading text has characters that a heading cannot hold') failed, so they were reverted. A 'vs' form changes the section id that the brief fixes (L905). Logged for the orchestrator with reader-08.

findings.section: Aurora Replicas read the shared volume so replica lag stays low (4 min), Stop and answer
findings.quote: No. Amazon RDS [copies them asynchronously to the read replica](../facts/rds.md#rds-read-replica-async-read-only) for each replica: one more replica is one more copy.
findings.evidence: The answer does not explain why a fourth replica leaves the lag unchanged: 'one more replica is one more copy' states a fact, not the cause. The cause she needs: each replica must apply every write it receives; lag comes from the write volume that each replica replays, and a fourth replica receives the same volume, so it lags the same. The sentence is also ungrammatical ('copies them ... for each replica'; 'them' has no antecedent). READER.md: depth means she can reason through an unseen question; STYLE.md one main idea per sentence.
findings.resolution: Answer now: 'No. Amazon RDS takes the primary's updates and [copies them asynchronously to the read replica]. Each replica replays every update, so a fourth replica lags the same.'

findings.section: FAQ quick-fire, FAQ 4; and Aurora Global Database copies the cluster volume to read-only Regions, Exam trap
findings.quote: **FAQ 4.** Can you create cross-Region replicas for Aurora?
findings.evidence: FAQ 4 answers 'Yes, with either physical or logical replication' (aurora-faq-cross-region-physical-or-logical), while the Global Database trap says 'Many think that Aurora PostgreSQL has a cross-Region read replica. It has no cross-Region Aurora Replicas, so use Aurora Global Database.' A reader who forgets the Aurora Replica / read replica distinction sees yes and no to the same question. Neither place says what 'logical replication' is, nor that Aurora MySQL has a cross-Region read replica (binlog; verified fact aurora-cmp-binlog-cross-region-replica-more-lag) while Aurora PostgreSQL has no cross-Region Aurora Replicas (aurora-postgres-no-cross-region-aurora-replicas). Add one sentence that reconciles them, or swap FAQ 4 for a brief alternate.
findings.resolution: The trap belief now names an Aurora Replica in another Region, and FAQ 4 adds 'Physical means Aurora Global Database.', so the two answers no longer conflict (same fix as claims-14). The Aurora MySQL binlog replica is not added (word cap; see exam-04).

findings.evidence: About 35 words with two clauses after a colon; STYLE.md: lint warns above 24 words, one main idea per sentence. The callout carries three traps in four sentences. Split into two sentences, or move the Serverless half to the Serverless v2 subsection.
findings.resolution: Split: 'Replicas do not remove I/O charges: I/O is [counted the same way] on writers and readers. Serverless v2 instances also use the [Aurora Standard or Aurora I/O-Optimized configuration].'
